entities.summary: William FitzWilliam, 1st Earl of Southampton, was an English courtier and soldier who played a significant role in the reign of King Henry VIII. Born into a noble family, FitzWilliam's early life was marked by his education at Oxford University and his service in various military campaigns against France and Scotland. He was appointed as the Earl of Southampton in 1538 and held this position until his death in 1542. During his tenure, FitzWilliam was a key advisor to King Henry VIII and participated in several important events, including the English Reformation and the dissolution of the monasteries. He also played a role in the court of King Henry VIII's second wife, Anne Boleyn, and was a close friend and ally of the English poet and playwright William Shakespeare. FitzWilliam's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the course of English history and played a significant role in the development of the modern English monarchy. His descendants continued to hold prominent positions in English society for centuries, including the 1st Duke of Albemarle, who was a prominent military leader and politician during the English Civil War.
